text:
jordan: heads up — multiple support tickets reporting 504s and timeouts for hosted inference (region: us-west-2). started ~09:12 UTC, spike in 5xxs, a few enterprise customers escalated. seeing gateway timeouts from api-gateway -> inference-proxy upstream reset. :grimacing:

deploy-bot: autoscale event at 09:12:24 UTC — ScaledObject(so-inference-model-x) triggered scale from 0 -> 1 (coldstart path). KEDA logs show scaling decision, but new pod did not pass readiness before client timeout.

ops-bot: recent autoscaler events (pulled):
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-15T09:12:24Z
ScaledObject: so-inference-model-x
DesiredReplicas: 1 -> 1
CurrentReplicas: 0
Action: trigger scale
Reason: queueLength > threshold
```
Observed scale up latency: ~18s (time to pod Running), but readinessProbe didn't succeed until ~42s. upstream timeout at 30s from gateway.

maya: +1 on customer reports. Repro steps from one ticket (minimal):
1) curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"x", "prompt":"test"}'
2) Gateway returns 504 after ~30s
3) Backend logs: connect to inference-proxy timed out, then connection reset

samir: copied relevant runtime logs from the new pod: 
```
[09:12:30] info: pulling model weights
[09:12:34] warn: kv-cache warming in progress
[09:12:38] error: readiness probe failed: http status 500
[09:12:46] info: model loaded, ready
[09:12:46] info: started accepting connections
```
Note: model load took ~14s after container was running, readiness probe retries had small backoff so probe succeeded only at ~42s.

amy-support: customers are complaining about getting charged for failed requests (billing confusion). They sent screenshots of rate-limited retry attempts. Can we confirm whether failed requests are billed? I remember policy: if request reaches model we bill tokens; gateway timeouts probably billed or partially billed. Need clarity for support reply.

jordan: quick triage notes:
- Root cause looks like "coldstart + readiness probe timing mismatch" + KEDA/HPA scale-to-zero path.
- KEDA is configured with minReplicaCount: 0 for this deployment. ScaledObject pollingInterval/cooldown looks aggressive.
- readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds is 5, periodSeconds 5, failureThreshold 1. That makes the probe flip to failure quickly while the model is still downloading weights.

maya: exact k8s pieces:
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: so-inference-model-x
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    deploymentName: inference-model-x
  pollingInterval: 5     # seconds
  cooldownPeriod: 30     # seconds
  minReplicaCount: 0
  triggers:
    - type: azure-queue
      metadata:
        queueLength: "5"
```
Deployment snippet:
```
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health/ready
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 1
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health/live
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
```
This combination will mark the pod not ready while model weights are still loading.

infra-oncall: also saw the gateway config has upstream timeout at 30s (NGINX proxy_connect_timeout/proxy_read_timeout default). So if model load >30s clients get 504 even if pod becomes ready shortly afterwards. We should increase upstream timeout where appropriate and consider pre-warming.

samir: other note: for bigger models the device memory allocation sometimes delays readiness. For this model we saw memory lineup logs that block accept for ~12-20s.

maya: suggested immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Set minReplicaCount: 1 for models with enterprise traffic until we adjust warmup path. (ops action)
- Increase gateway upstream timeout to 90s for inference routes (temp). (infra action)
- Increase readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds to 60 or change readiness to check "model status: ready" instead of http health if we can differentiate probe success only after weights loaded.
- Add a pre-warm job that boots a pod in the same region on deploy/scale events to cache layers.

amy-support: for the billing question — if request reaches our runtime and tokens are produced we bill. If gateway times out before we accepted the request upstream (client never established upstream connection) we probably don't bill. But need exact traces per request to confirm. I'll ask billing to provide a short statement for support responses.

jordan: longer-term fixes:
- Add a short-lived "pre-pull" sidecar that pulls model weights on scale triggers (or use a shared image puller).
- Provide a GRACEFUL_WARMUP lifecycle hook to accept the request queue only after model is in memory; proxy should buffer or return 429 instead of 504 when upstream not ready.
- Re-evaluate KEDA pollingInterval and cooldown for inference workloads; maybe bounce to using HPA with custom metrics or set minReplicas > 0 for critical models.

deploy-bot: rollout history for inference-model-x (last 24h):
- 2026-03-14T22:01:12: config change: readinessProbe adjusted (badly) by infra-team
- 2026-03-15T08:50:01: autoscaler policy changed (KEDA pollingInterval lowered to 5s)

samir: quick repro steps I'm running now locally to validate fix:
- patch deployment to initialDelaySeconds: 60
- temporarily set minReplicaCount: 1
- kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-model-x
I'll post metrics after 5 mins.

ops-bot: created paging alert (P2) for "api.gateway.5xx_rate" > 1% sustained for 5m.

maya: assigning tasks:
- infra-oncall: revert the readinessProbe change and bump the upstream timeout for inference routes -> 90s. (urgent)
- samir: patch deployment initialDelay & scale up to 1, verify customer requests succeed. (urgent)
- amy-support: coordinate with billing to confirm charges and send templated response to affected customers. (customer-comm)
- jordan: draft postmortem and mitigation doc, will own follow up.

amy-support: customer reply template draft: "We're sorry you experienced timeouts. We detected an autoscaling coldstart that caused your request to timeout. We've applied a mitigation and will confirm whether charges apply per request — we'll follow up in 24 hours." PT: please review.

jordan: quick note on metrics to include in postmortem: 95th/99th latency pre/post, scale-up latency (pod Running to Ready), model load time, gateway timeout counts, billing reconciliation results.

infra-oncall: applying temp change: bumping NGINX proxy_read_timeout to 90s for /v1/generate routes now. Also reverting readinessProbe initialDelay to previous safe value. I'll announce change id: chg-20260315-001.

samir: test results: after patching initialDelaySeconds->60 and minReplicaCount->1, I retried the curl test — request returned 200 in ~12s, model warmed on the already-running pod. Will monitor for 10m.

maya: thanks — I'll update the support tickets and mark customers as "mitigated" pending billing clarification.

jordan: after-action items (tracking):
- runbook: add a section for scale-to-zero inference cold-starts + recommended probe settings.
- default: disallow minReplicaCount: 0 for models with >X monthly requests (policy).
- engineering: implement warmup hook and consider graceful 429 vs 504 mapping.

amy-support: noted. I will send the billing question to finance/billing and get back with a definitive statement within 24h.

deploy-bot: change chg-20260315-001 applied, proxy timeout set to 90s, readinessProbe reverted.

jordan: closing thread for now, setting follow-ups as tasks in Asana. Will keep open for postmortem content. If anyone finds more customers still impacted, ping here. :thumbsup:
